messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] SLO breach detected - streaming endpoint /v1/stream (us-west-2)
• p95=0.92s (target 0.6s)
• p99=1.83s (target 0.9s)
• error: streaming stalls / tail latency spikes, clients seeing stalled chunks (~3-6s hang)
• affected pool: inference-usw2-gpu-pool-7 (models: redwood-vicuna-16b-* variants)
• hot nodes observed: gpu-node-02f, gpu-node-02g
• anomaly: ECC correctable error rate rising on gpu-node-02f, thermal throttle events on same host
PagerDuty: severity P1, page routed to #oncall (ryan) — runbook: https://runbooks.internal/incidents/streaming-tail

oncall-ryan: ack — looking now. grabbing logs & nvml metrics. will post quick checks.

eng-sre-alia: thanks — tagging in. initial suspicion: hardware-level correction spikes causing micro-stalls in kernel leading to KV cache pipeline stalls for streaming.

infra-tom: pulling nvml and dmesg from gpu-node-02f now. preliminary: correctable ECCs ramping up, device reports thermal events. short snippet from dmesg:
```
[2026-03-15T14:02:10Z] NVRM: ECC_CORRECTABLE: gpu-02f count 24 -> 102 within 5m
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] GPU_THERMAL: GPU 02f temp 86C, throttle_count++
[2026-03-15T14:02:20Z] driver: resetting hw queue for gpu-02f
```
this matches the p99 tail windows.

oncall-ryan: running live checks:
```
kubectl get pods -n inference -l pool=usw2-gpu-pool-7 -o wide
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu,memory.used,ecc.errors.corrected --format=csv -i 02
```
I see streaming replicas pinned to gpu-node-02f and 02g.

support-maya: support reports two customers complaining about multi-chunk streaming stalls between 13:58-14:07 UTC (us-west). one is on Dedicated, one Hosted. both saw client timeouts and retransmits. tickets #12345 & #12346 opened.

eng-sre-alia: live mitigation proposals (short list):
1) immediate: avoid scheduling new work on gpu-node-02f/02g (taint + cordon).
2) scale up fallback pool (cpu-fallback or alternate gpu pool) and route a fraction of traffic to it (can increase token cost but reduces stalls).
3) enable model variant fallback to quantized 8-bit variant for streaming to reduce kernel stress.
4) if stalls persist, enable per-request small-chunk-size streaming to reduce KV pressure.

oncall-ryan: doing 1 & 2 now.

deploybot: Action: scaling cpu-fallback-pool replicas 3 -> 6 (automated).
deploybot: Action: updating routing: add temporary route rule to divert 20% of streaming traffic from pool-7 to cpu-fallback-pool (policy: tail-mitigation-7912468001).

oncall-ryan: cordon & drain in progress for gpu-node-02f:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-02f
kubectl drain gpu-node-02f --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m
kubectl label node gpu-node-02f redwood/gpu_flaky=true
```
drain shows some streaming pods stuck in terminating — likely blocked on gRPC streams. manually killing long-running stream workers with `--force` to free kernels.

infra-tom: confirming ECC counts increased again after drain start:
```
[2026-03-15T14:04:48Z] ECC_CORRECTABLE: gpu-02f count 102 -> 138
thermal_temp=88C throttle_count=5
```
hardware vendor ticket being prepared — may require board swap.

product-jess: can we get a short customer-facing blurb? ops: ETA on mitigation?

support-maya: mitigation in place: routing change + scale up. early telemetry shows p99 dropping from 1.83s -> ~1.1s for routed traffic; clients on diverted pool report fewer stalls. ETA for complete drain of gpu-node-02f ~8-12m.

eng-sre-alia: good. next step: quarantine node and force replacement schedule. also follow-up action to add kernel-level watchdog for stream workers to preempt stalls on node-level ECC spikes.

ops-lina: heads-up — I'm on the next shift starting in 20m, @oncall-ryan can you handoff the ongoing incident to me once drain completes? I'll monitor the fallback route and customer comms.

oncall-ryan: yup — I'll hand off after we confirm p99 steady under 1.0s for 5m and drain finished. leaving notes in the incident channel and PD.

deploybot: Update: scaled fallback pool -> completed, traffic rule applied.

infra-tom: node gpu-node-02f is now drained and quarantined (label applied). collecting full nvml logs and packing into attachment for vendor.

support-maya: sending customer update draft: "We detected elevated retry and tail latency on streaming in us-west. We routed traffic to a fallback pool and are replacing a degraded GPU node. There may be short increases in latency while mitigation finishes. We'll follow up with a post-incident report."

product-jess: looks good, please include affected customers list and timeline in the postmortem.

eng-sre-alia: quick post-incident checklist items:
- Confirm rollback / fallback durations and exact p95/p99 graphs (Observability).
- Vendor HW ticket + device replacement ETA.
- Runbook update: add steps for forced termination of stuck streaming workers during drains.
- Add alert threshold: ECC correctables > 50/min for a node -> auto-taint/evacuate.

oncall-ryan: handing off to ops-lina. summary: root cause likely hardware ECC + thermal causing intermittent kernel stalls -> streaming tail latency. mitigation: drained & quarantined gpu-node-02f, scaled fallback pool, applied temporary routing rule and model-variant fallback. customers notified, tickets opened.

ops-lina: taking over. monitoring. will open the incident postmortem and assign owners for HW ticket, runbook changes, and observability dashboards.

incident-bot: Incident status updated: mitigated -> partial (P1->P2), monitoring. postmortem link placeholder: https://runbooks.internal/incidents/7912468001/postmortem

support-maya: posted customer update to ticket threads.

eng-sre-alia: note for follow-up: check streaming chunk size heuristics — some workloads benefit from 128-token chunking instead of 512 to avoid long tail stalls.

ops-lina: thanks all — closing the live paging loop. we'll schedule hardware swap and follow up with a proper RCA and timeline. :white_check_mark:
